summary: Sweep project documentation against current code and retained evidence; correct stale status, recovery ownership, ZFS capability, delivery and website claims while preserving historical limits. API impact: existing contract; reference descriptions clarified without changing runtime behaviour.

guide.reason: Correct current scope, driver media, storage capabilities, pool/recovery availability and delivery instructions against implementation; prior walkthrough limits retained.

api.reason: Clarify existing ZFS provisioned/shared/per-host/outcome semantics against current Controller/Core handlers and protocol types. No endpoint, payload validation, authentication, authorization, command or result behaviour changed.

roadmap.reason: Keep incomplete convergence and master-recovery work open and distinguish bounded development checks from publication.

state.reason: Documentation, reference descriptions and static website text only; no runtime state added. Existing pool records remain Core-owned; Controller remains a relay and observed-state projection.

verification.method: Parallel source/evidence review, API contract/generation checks, website check/build and real local browser walkthrough, local link inspection and documentation/privacy gates. The website hardening browser script now reads its optional host-resolver address from NEX_WEBSITE_RESOLVE_IP with a reserved documentation default instead of a hard-coded deployment address; verified with python3 -m py_compile and git grep for the removed literal, and the script is not run with --resolve in either workflow. Independent review and exact results/limits are recorded in the sweep report.
